This was a certified good game (TM)! Yeah, sure, it was nothing special, but it was all in good fun and had a lot of replayability due to the endless mode (which I did not try) and the RNG and the 6 unique cats. Plus, you can place the lightbulbs in any order you want and pick up any furniture you want! The story/plot only takes up about a quarter of the game, so the gameplay's the main star of show, and boy does it work!

It's one of the 2 tower defense games I actually enjoyed (the other is Plants vs. Zombies), mainly due to the uniqueness, the close-knit, homey vibes that I can't really put into words, and the feeling of building your own homemade, childhood fort! It feels very real and grounded and just... fun.

I did not play the endless mode. If I did, this is where I would put the review for it.

Some of the furniture given did feel a little underpowered/overpowered. The toaster, for example, is basically useless, while the bubble blower and yarn tosser are amazing and perfect to get early game and Catnip felt just a little underwhelming. I went through the game from Laundry->Bottom Room->The Other Room, incase you were curious, so that may have affected my tastes a little.

The ending segment felt like a great culmination of all the characters involved. Wondering what those characters and their roles are? Buy the game and read Grandpa's diary! Still, the end segment was fun, but it felt too different, but maybe that was an intro to endless mode. I dunno because I never played it, so maybe it was, but I personally thought it was out of place, so whatever.

All in all, it's great, but it's not worth 8.99$. It feels a lot like a Game Jam Game than a full-fledged independent game. It's worth moreso 5.99$. I'd say you should get it during a discount. Still a great game, but a little too overpriced for my tastes.

A charming and fairly short fort building game. Defend a young girl as she tries to read a book against an onslaught of cats that want to sit on her lap. Adorable.

The game features a light story about a girl going to visit her grandparents, but they're nowhere to be seen when she arrives. She finds her grandfather's journal, sits down to read it, and keeps getting interrupted by cats. Clearly, the solution is to build a cat proof fort. To do so, you arrange various objects in defensive positions around the sitting character. As the game progresses, you'll unlock a wide variety of objects to defend against a wide variety of types of cats that fly at your base.

The story mode of the game is brief, 2 hours or so, after which you unlock a challenge mode that you can keep playing. The story isn't particularly difficult, and once you get the hang of building a fort, the stages don't differentiate from each other very much. It's a pretty light game.

[b]Basic Breakdown[/b]: Fort Meow is a fort building/tower defense puzzle game with physics. Developed by [b]Upper Class Walrus[/b] and published by [b]Surprise Attack[/b].

Upon finding her grandfather’s journal in the attic, that she wandered up to while waiting for him to return home. Nia is attacked by a barrage of felines desperately trying to keep her from peacefully reading said journal. It seems that her grandmother has become a crazy cat lady since last time she visited, so you are tasked with defending Nia by building a protective fort out of furniture you find within the house to keep the cats at bay, while deciphering the mysterious tales hidden within the journal and uncovering the secrets behind these seemingly endless feline lap attacks.

[b]Graphics[/b]: Quite cute, character designs are adorably unique which adds to the unique premise and story of the game. I love the design of the house with it capturing something of a ''this is not all it seems to be'' vibe. I'd say this could run on any type of PC with ease even at the highest setting. 

[b]Soundtrack[/b]: For the initial waves going through the story it's mostly the same sort of track with mild variations, it can get a little bit annoying, but it makes for a nice background track while you're building your fort... However, the ending track is an absolute masterpiece. Was honestly worth playing through the whole game just for the final soundtrack!

[b]Menu[/b]: Extremely simplistic. Sliders for sound controls, resolution arrow keys and a full-screen/windowed tick box. Has what you need and offers it to you an a really simple, but well done way.

[b]Final Conclusion[/b]: I'm most definitely glad I picked this little gem up, it gave me quite a bit of entertainment and a little bit of rage. It's adorable and quirky with a really different story-line that can be enjoyed at any age. It's simplistic enough that it could run on any kind of potato PC and still be smooth.

The added physics make it tricky to account for and add a strategic element to builds. Been one centimeter off protecting your fort from being penetrated by a fat cat or melon head cat makes it just that little bit frustrating that you almost had it, and thus making you motivated to try again and continue playing.

Once finishing the main story-line you have, of course, an endless mode which gives you fish tokens to buy outfits for Nia, new cat types and yarn. I actually quite like this as it can still keep you playing and entertained for quite some time. 

All in all, I'm definitely giving this game a thumbs up.

This game was so fun! It's really entertaining watching the cats fling themselves at the fort. This game isn't too tough, but it's not so simple that you'll succeed the first time every time, either. You have to make strategic choices about what cat-deterrant products to try (a shoe box that can trap a single cat, or a basket of laundry that might yield extra clothes as additional cushioning?). There's also a fun story that's slowly revealed as you progress through the rounds (the story of "what the heck is up with all these cats, anyway?"), which is great incentive to keep going. I lost interest after story mode (there's also an endless "challenge" mode), but that's fine. I like games I can finish, and I'm really glad I played this one. It's fun, funny, cute, and entertaining for an evening or two.

While it is a little hard to understand why you wouldn't want a cat in your lap while you read, avoiding that is the goal of 'Fort Meow'.  A goal achieved by using household to items build a protective fort to outlast waves of feline assailants.

The game's theme is solidified by strong visual and audio design.  Stacking physics works well making fort building is enjoyable.  It would benefit from showing more information on cat attack waves along with the ability to save fort designs.  On occasion the physics interactions make winning or losing appear to depend on luck over skill.

[h1]Ziel/Story[/h1]
Nia (der Spieler) findet ein von ihrem Großvater geschriebenes Buch und möchte es lesen. Doch jedes mal sobald sie anfängt, fliegen aus allen Richtungen Katzen heran um auf ihrem Schoß Platz zu nehmen. Echt nervig! DAS muss geändert werden und so beginnt das ganze Spiel. Baut mit allen Gegenständen, die ihr auf dem Dachboden oder im späteren Spielverlauf in den Zimmern des Hauses findet eine Kissenburg, die der Katzenbelagerung standhält.

[h1]Steuerung[/h1]
Man benötigt an sich nur die Maus (Links- und Rechtsklick sowie Mausrad zum Drehen der Gegenstände). Zum Drehen der Gegenstände können alternativ die Pfeiltasten verwendet werden. --> Einfach und simpel. Das sollte jeder hinkriegen.

[h1]Achievements[/h1]
An sich logisch zum Spiel aufgebaut: einige bekommt man während des Spielverlaufs. Andere lassen sich nach Beenden des Spiels noch schnell abräumen oder in einer neuen kurzen Runde bzw. im Endlosmodus. Das Endlosspiel wird nach erstmaligem Beenden des Storymodes freigeschaltet.

[h1]Bugs/Probleme[/h1]
Mir sind zwei Dinge aufgefallen: Bevor ich das Game erstmals abgeschlossen habe musste ich auf den Desktop zurücktabben und dann per Rechtsklick in der Taskleiste das Spiel beenden. Irgendwie funktionierte das Zurückschalten auf das Menü nicht. Zum Glück speichert das Spiel automatisch ab, wodurch der Spielfluss nicht behindert wird und nach dem ersten Durchspielen funktionierten die Schaltflächen wieder. Das Zweite ist mir aufgefallen, als ich während das Spiel geöffnet war jemanden in einer PN antworten wollte: Ich kann im Tab-Menü nichts anklicken. Aber dann halt wieder zurück auf den Desktop, Steam auswählen und halt so antworten. Mich hats nicht wirklich gestört (ich bin bei sowas glaube ich viel zu entspannt um mich aufzuregen), wollte es aber der Vollständigkeit mal erwähnen.

[h1]Bewertung[/h1]
Dafür, dass Fort Meow ein relativ kleines und einfaches Spiel ist, wurde wert auf eine solide, herzerwärmende und doch lustige Geschichte gelegt, die nach und nach erforscht wird. Die Kissenburgen lassen sich in unzähligen Varianten errichten und können dem eigenen Spielstil angepasst werden (Defensiv, Aggressiv, Passiv-Aggressiv). Das taktische Können wird auch ein wenig abgefragt, da es verschiedene Katzentypen gibt und sie unterschiedliche Eigenschaften haben (z. B. schneller heftiger Schaden oder doppelter Schaden), für welche man bestimmte Gegenstände einsetzen sollte. Die Optik ist nicht überragend, aber definitiv alles andere als schlecht! Ich hatte viel Freude dabei die unterschiedlichen Katzenarten, Gegenstände und Charakter zu betrachten. Ich muss zugeben, ich habe das Spiel im Sale gekauft und den Besitz nicht bereut. Für Zwischendurch ein wunderbares Spiel :-)

It promotes a pointless genocide of cats who would rather just be left alone to dream of electric mice, all for the amusement of asinine children. The grandfather's approach to them (that can be gleaned from the journal) is also highly controversial to me - how he treats them as disposable objects, not noticing a point past which they no longer were such. And back to the kids again - it's all fun and smiles for them while the (clearly at least semi-sentient) cats are fighting desperately for survival. The callousness of the whole thing left me disturbed and saddened, from a casual game I would've never suspected of influencing me in such a way.

This game is a purrrrfect casual delight!

If you're a cat person, or enjoy strategic defense games, puzzle games, or physics based games, or even if you think this game looks mildly interesting; buy it.  The definition of what this game is exactly is a little bit difficult to nail down.  Part of me wants to call it akin to a tower defense game, but it isn’t, there aren’t really any ‘towers’ per say.  Part of me wants to call it a casual game, but it isn’t, there’s more than enough challenging game play to satisfy.  Part of me wants to call it a puzzle game, but it isn’t, it’s got a lot of ways to ‘solve’ each level.

So here’s what I can say it is for sure;  

This game is a unique twist on strategic ‘base defense’.  The attacks come in the form of cats that want to sit on your lap and cuddle with you while you’re trying to read.  That’s right, if you ‘lose’ you have the pleasure of being treated to a kitty on your lap and a purring sound.  It completely negates the sting of any loss instantly.  There is a bit of a challenge in trying to get your base, which by the way is akin to a child’s pillow fort, set up exactly the way you want it before feline nemesis come and knock it down.

The music is great and fits the game very well.  The graphics are cute and well done, mildly akin to scribblenauts, without actually looking like them.  The gameplay is simple and at no point was I ever confused about what to do.

Also, for those who really want to push their skill, there are a multitude of ‘power ups’ that are actually quite tricky to use at the right moment.  But I’ve done the whole game so far without using one, focusing on building my pillow fort to exact details.  In fact if I have any complaint, it’s that the cats come a little too fast to use many of the power ups with confidence.

I am blown away how much I, as a middle aged man, have enjoyed this obviously child’s game.  But I can tell I’m going to be putting quite a few hours in on this one.

If you like pillow forts and funny cats there's a good chance you will like this game.  Just be sure you're okay with it being silly instead of a serious engineering simulation.

The Good:
[list]
[*] It is more cerebral than it might appear.  Most items do something other than take a beating, and you need to think about how the fort will collapse over time to cause it to intercept enemies effectively.
[/list]

The Bad:
[list]
[*] The physics engine is non-deterministic.  The same exact fort (the game restores your build if it crumbles) may fail one time, and succeed another, depending on your luck.  This is the only thing keeping the game from being played more seriously.
[*] The ‘active defenses’ (like the toaster that fires toast at random intervals in random arcs) are too slow, unpredictable, and costly to be of much use.  That's a pity, because several are fun to play with.
[*] The tightly timed last level is more frustrating than fun.  The clunky controls are normally fine, but really make this level hard to beat.
[*] I felt a bit sorry for the stolen animals and robot cats in the end.  Grandpa doesn't seem so nice.
[/list]
